"Double The Money" has 188,883 prizes of $10 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $2,000 prize, with two left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

If "Double The Money" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2415.headline: What's actually left to win

2416.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Loaded with $2,000s", about a third are still unsold. The game is well into its run, with 1,240 of 3,372 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Everything above about "Loaded with $2,000s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2416.headline: Early stage or late

2419.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "Bronze 7s" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Tomorrow's count on "Bronze 7s" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
2419.headline: Early stage or late

2420.body:
"Silver 7s" has gone three weeks without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About half of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $177,777 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

If you play "Silver 7s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2420.headline: Three weeks, no top prize claimed

2421.body:
"Gold 7s" has fewer top prizes left. The count changed when one top prize of $577,777 was claimed over a week ago. Unsold tickets still hold one of the original three. Check the top prize count first when you compare scratchers.

Everything here about "Gold 7s" comes from official Virginia lottery numbers, current through November 10.
2421.headline: Another top prize was claimed

2422.body:
The prize money on "Platinum 7s" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $2 million. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Everything above about "Platinum 7s" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2422.headline: The prize mix in this game

2426.body:
"HAUNTED HUNDREDS" has 2,136 of 5,340 top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Today's free summary of "HAUNTED HUNDREDS" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2426.headline: Tickets sold so far

2427.body:
"HOLIDAY TRIPLER" has 556 of 602 top prizes left and is early in its run. Only a small slice of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, tickets and top prizes are running out at about the same rate.

The table below shows the full count for "HOLIDAY TRIPLER", with every prize level included.
2427.headline: Tickets sold so far

2428.body:
The most common win left on "PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" is $2. The second biggest prize left is $500, and 65 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

If you play "PEPPERMINT PAYOUT" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
2428.headline: What the prize table shows

2429.body:
MERRY MONEY TREE's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $500. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

The numbers for "MERRY MONEY TREE" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2429.headline: Where the prize money is

2430.body:
The key fact about "WRAPPED IN RICHES" is how its ten prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

Everything above about "WRAPPED IN RICHES" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
